Rate limiting is global via ANONYMOUS_ORG, so one account can lock out all users. It should be per-account by email instead. Throttled accounts are refused even with the correct password. Reset requests are limited independently per address. Remember me has no effect; sessions always last 30 days. The login flow double-charges rate limits because both loginAction and login() consume the same quota.

I will restore a per-token rate limit in the service. This keeps the confirm path from sharing the global request quota. The original code threw "Too many reset attempts" when the global bucket was exhausted, which broke tests that expected one email to work while another was throttled.

I will leave the confirm path unthrottled. The spec exempts sign-in throttling, so completing a password reset after reset-request throttle is reasonable. The request service returns silently when rate-limited, but the action throws.
